Title: The Yellow Wallpaper
Author: Charlotte Perkins Stetson
My Review:
the bars on the window? i think the room is kind of a place where you isolate people. obvious duh tbh
i couldn't comprehend it at first, the ending was too ambiguous and unsettling, it gave me chills.
There is a woman in wallpaper and the woman likes to go outside, bask in sun and sit on grass, and same does the author. the woman in wallpaper is the author, stuck in confinement and patriarchal authority, so what does it mean when her husband and his sister were somewhat skeptical of the wallpaper? and why it has to be her to rip the wallpaper and no one else? DID SHE KILL HERSELF!!??? that's why husband couldn't hear when she said where the key was, or husband was a man that's why he couldn't. and she kept creeping (btw there were bars on the window)

husband wanted to cure her, also telling her that she is fine and not sick, her brother too, but did it in such a way that killed her. he restricted her.

> we go round and round: does that means confined, domestic, opressed?

> I kept on creeping just the same, but I looked at him over my shoulder: earlier she watched the woman creep and now she is the woman.

> I kept creeping over him.

where did this story took a huge turn to display such impact of patriarchy on women? i can't understand but i like this one. there are layers which need a deep search within oneself.

Title: Notes from Underground
Author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
Additional Authors: Richard Pevear, Donald Fanger, Larissa Volokhonsky
My Review:
Picked it up and dropped it down MULTIPLE times. English is not my strong point and p&v makes it a bit harder with its 'grandioseness'. idk if that word exists. but one day a certain concept of "ending what I start" miraculously appeared (or maybe I learned it from life) appeared and boom. restarted and end this book.

Now a bit about this book and my incompetency.
I had a hard time understanding it and still maybe I'm much of a kid to this vast depth full of characters. Although not "understanding" this novel, I can say Dostoevsky is a Genius with his characters. and about "my incompetency", it emerges from an idea that I must understand a certain character from his roots. from his simplest words, from his name to his death, from the first principles. Which leaves with this sudden savoury taste in my tongue after reading the novel, I can't blame myself yk.
nvm. my yap can go on unfortunately forever.

wait

maybe there's some similarities between me and Dostoevsky (we all have one). I like him. for his genius. adore him. he will forever be my favourite.

Everyone should read this book to get a glimpse of the void and find how shallow of a person they are. But alas they'll always be like that until a change emerges from within. and that will never happen. nature reverts back to its natural form. we all are nature. that idea of "beautiful and lofty" is drawing me. I call it art. dostoevsky's "beautiful and lofty" is what I call "Art".

I have yapped on for quite long. Maybe I will write a blog post on this one. this book has definitely changed me for the better.

will reread once I am more mature. which is. once per year 😊

Title: The Death of Ivan Ilych
Author: Leo Tolstoy
My Review:
I must say how one has an understanding of the END? Tuesdays with Morrie. One of the books which had influenced me very well, and now this one by Tolstoy.

He was content with the vessel he called life which he moulded himself, later regretting it. The relation he made with the external environment but so helpless before his death full of questions. At the end he gradually accepted. not every question is answered and everything is uncertain. seeing death since childhood I've become indifferent to that. Accepted it's a part of life but now, reading a first hand perspective from an author who was alive when he wrote this (duh! 🙄), I'm not me. This shallow brain of mine can't process. There are multiple thought processes and tracing one of them seems a bit hard.

The perspective of Ivan during the end was one which affected me the most. One is happy and then becomes sad to not be happy again until the environment changes. Life certainly is a series of suffering stacking up. How do one navigate it is unknown to everyone.

I would recommend this short book to everyone. A must read for everyone once during his lifetime. what can go wrong reading a 60 pages short book?

My ADHD can speedrun faster than this, writing a book 'kits thought after tolstoy' so I'll stop. disclaimer: I am new to writing and my brain is still immature to understand this delicacy of life. Sensitivity of the brain. and inhumanity of people. literally everything and have much to learn about everything. wow this turned into my blog page haha.

This is (one tenth of) what I am thinking after reading this book.
